UI_NMS_Help: <H1> Nutrition <LINE> <TEXT> Food does three things: it fills your <RGB:0.86,0.76,0.52> stomach <RGB:1,1,1> , it tops up your <RGB:0.95,0.72,0.35> energy <RGB:1,1,1> , and it supplies <RGB:0.62,0.78,0.58> protein <RGB:1,1,1> . Food tooltips show all three as pips. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Stomach <LINE> <TEXT> One pip is about one hour of fullness. Bulky, fatty and protein-rich food keeps you full longer than sugary snacks with the same calories. While your stomach has food in it you are Well Fed and wounds heal a little faster. A stomach holds about five hours; eating past that is wasted. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Hunger <LINE> <TEXT> Hunger returns gradually as the stomach empties, and faster when your energy reserve is low. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Energy <LINE> <TEXT> One pip is about 250 kcal. Hard work burns more. A small surplus is stored as fat and a deficit is drawn from fat, so your weight follows what you eat over weeks. Below zero your body is running on empty and malnourishment builds. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Protein <LINE> <TEXT> One pip is about 10 g. Protein slowly runs down every day. Meat, fish, eggs, beans, nuts and dairy restore it. Staying deficient causes malnourishment even if you eat enough calories. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Malnourishment <LINE> <TEXT> Builds over days when you are short on calories or protein, and fades over a day or two once you eat properly. It slows stamina recovery and healing. The faint bar shows where it is heading. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Weight <LINE> <TEXT> Changes slowly. The coloured bands are where weight traits change: underweight below 75 kg, overweight above 85 kg.
